US_counterstrike.source: TG58.1/TG58.3 after return-bearing/search localization of Japanese four-carrier force
US_counterstrike.CAP_note: First-line CAP plus limited rear-deck relay/recovery depth; no fixed-base A-grade GCI bonus at sea.

centered_damage.Hiryu: One bomb hit plus damaging near miss centered; flight operations stop for the day, propulsion/waterline integrity retained.
centered_damage.Soryu: Light splinter/near-miss damage centered; continues flight operations at reduced efficiency.

carrier_air_cumulative_2Feb.note: Japanese total includes offensive strike plus CAP/recon losses; local Marshall land-air losses are accounted separately.

Marshall_afternoon.reason: Carrier exchange diverts/desynchronizes part of the second-day TF58 suppression wallet; Gilbert land air continues.

state_T24.C2: Taroa/Roi mostly C+/C with intermittent local warning; water-air/rear nodes preserve some search and night movement.

fleet_decisions.Japan: No second carrier strike. After recovery, Hiryu deck loss and heavy cadre attrition, Yamamoto turns west under CAP/rear-deck recovery cover.
fleet_decisions.US: No immediate deep chase. Cabot is campaign-out, Intrepid temporarily deck-limited, island suppression and amphibious timetable remain priority. Ten fast decks remain available once Intrepid recovers.

state_2FebT24.Japanese_first_line: Shokaku/Zuikaku/Soryu operational; Hiryu flight operations disabled pending short repair assessment. Surviving air groups heavily cross-decked/reorganized.
state_2FebT24.Japanese_secondary: Four rear decks remain intact and absorb orphan aircraft/recovery load; they do not erase aircrew cadre debt.
state_2FebT24.US_TF58: Cabot out; Intrepid expected to recover near-normal deck cycle on a short clock if structural inspection is clean; other fast decks combat operational.
state_2FebT24.D_day: 1944-02-06 remains centerline; no automatic move yet.
